sources: recreation.gov public campsite search API for 232327 (per-site catalog), read 2026-10-22

values.note: $15 per site per night in every 2026 season; additional vehicle $5 per night.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/spring-gulch-campground ('Single Site: $15 per night Additional Vehicle: $5 per night') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232327/rates (2026 Walk-Up Season, Peak Season and September: STANDARD NONELECTRIC and RV NONELECTRIC 15), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Forest Service: 'Historically, campground will open early May and close at the end of September.' Peak season Memorial Day - Labor Day; off-peak opening depends on weather and spring river conditions (call the Darby Ranger Station, 406-821-3913). recreation.gov's 2026 rate seasons ran May 15 - September 30.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/spring-gulch-campground (Current Conditions: 'Historically, campground will open early May and close at the end of September'; Seasons of Use: 'Peak season is Memorial Day - Labor Day. Non-peak season is dependent on weather and spring river conditions'), read 2026-10-22

hookups.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232327 ('RV hookups are not available'; every site in the catalog typed NONELECTRIC), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 10 sites plus a bicycle site; single and double-family sites. The Forest Service says trailers and RVs to 50 ft; recreation.gov lists site lengths of 20-65 ft.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/spring-gulch-campground ('hosts 10 sites, plus 1 bicycle site ... Campground can accommodate trailers and RVs to 50'') + recreation.gov catalog for 232327 (Max Vehicle Length 20-65), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Potable water and garbage service during peak season only. Accessible fishing pier on the river; picnic area.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/spring-gulch-campground ('vault toilets', 'Garbage service and potable water is provided during peak season', 'a fishing pier on the river') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232327 ('accessible vault toilets and drinking water'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Forest Service-run (Sula/Darby Ranger District). recreation.gov sells 5 of the 11 overnight sites; the other 6 are first-come, and the rate table runs walk-up seasons outside July 1 - Labor Day. Reservations close 4 days before arrival. Camping limited to 16 consecutive days. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232327 (rules: reservationCutOff 4 'day(s) prior to arrival', maxConsecutiveStay 16) + recreation.gov catalog (5 reservable, 6 non-reservable overnight sites) + /rates (2026 'Walk-Up Season' May 15 - June 30, 'Peak Season' July 1 - Sept 6, walk-in rates Sept 7-30) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/spring-gulch-campground ('Camping limited to 16 consecutive days'; 'Check Out: Noon Check In: 2:00pm'), read 2026-10-22

note: Bitterroot NF (Sula RD) on the East Fork Bitterroot River, 3 mi NW of Sula on US-93 (~75 mi S of Missoula); grassy ponderosa pine, single and double sites, accessible fishing pier. recreation.gov warns of potential closures from springtime flooding. --Claude
summary: Forest Service page + recreation.gov: confirmed $15 (2026), no hookups, 10 sites (+bike site), 50-ft rigs, vault toilets, seasonal water, reservable on recreation.gov (derived values now verified). Added fcfs some_sites (6 of 11 first-come, walk-up seasons), 4-day reservation cutoff, 16-night limit, season closing end of September (opens 'early May', weather-dependent). FS-run, no concessionaire. FS page shows 'Site Closed' (seasonal, October). No current FS alert for the campground or US-93.
flags: Missing phone: the Forest Service and recreation.gov give 406-821-3913 (Darby/Sula Ranger District) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/spring-gulch-campground).
